rows.note: The board is the screen that hurts most: six lists in one page, each needing its own slice of the same table.

rows.Rayfold: 1: the read op refers to the write op with `$ref`, and the server runs them in order

rows.aspect: A write and the two screens that show it
rows.metric: round trips for a write plus two screens
rows.REST: 3: one for the write, one for the board, one for the feed
rows.GraphQL: 2: a document is a mutation or a query, never both, so the screens follow the write
rows.Rayfold: 1: writes and reads are ops of the same batch, run in order, and rows loaded for one op are not loaded again for the next
rows.note: Within the request the server keeps what it loaded: the people on the board are not fetched a second time for the feed.

rows.aspect: Lost update refused (two writers, one issue)
rows.unit: the losing writer gets the current row back (1 = yes)
rows.REST: 412 with the current representation in the body, because this endpoint was written to include it
rows.GraphQL: an error with a code and the current version number; the row itself needs another request
rows.Rayfold: a typed `VersionConflict` carrying the current entity in the shape the op asked for, so the client can redraw and retry without a read
rows.note: All three refuse the stale write. The difference is what the client has to do next.

request.body: {"query":"mutation { updateIssue(id: \"i003\", patch: { title: \"Renamed by the first writer\" }, ifVersion: 1) { version } }"}

response.body: {"data":{"updateIssue":{"version":2}}}

request.body: {"query":"mutation { updateIssue(id: \"i003\", patch: { title: \"Renamed by the second writer\" }, ifVersion: 1) { version } }"}

response.body: {"errors":[{"message":"Issue i003 is at version 2","locations":[{"line":1,"column":12}],"path":["updateIssue"],"extensions":{"code":"CONFLICT","actual":2}}],"data":null}
{"id":1,"ok":{"$type":"Issue","version":2},"patch":[],"meta":{"cost":1},"fin":true}

request.body: {"ops":[{"id":1,"op":"updateIssue","args":{"id":"i003","patch":{"title":"Renamed by the second writer"}},"key":"ws-edit-00000002","ifVersion":1,"shape":"{ key title version }"}]}

response.body: {"id":1,"error":{"code":"failed_precondition","message":"Issue:i003 is at version 2, not 1","type":"VersionConflict","data":{"key":"Issue:i003","expected":1,"actual":2,"current":{"$type":"Issue","key":"ING-3","title":"Renamed by the first writer","version":2}}},"fin":true}

rows.unit: changed rows the write itself reports
rows.metric: what the client learns from the write
rows.REST: the new sprint state. Which of the cached issues moved is not said, so the client refetches the lists it holds
rows.GraphQL: whatever the mutation selected. A mutation cannot describe rows it did not return, so the client refetches
rows.Rayfold: 11 entity patches plus the sprint, in the command's own answer: every cached screen holding those issues is corrected with no further request
rows.note: The sprint held 11 unfinished issues. Patches are part of every command's answer, not something the server was asked for.

rows.metric: what it takes to keep one screen correct
rows.REST: an SSE endpoint, an event fan-out and client merge code; the event carries an id, so the client refetches (1,090 B to become correct)
rows.GraphQL: a Subscription type, a resolver with an async iterator, and client merge code; then a refetch (225 B)
rows.Rayfold: `live: true` on the query that already draws the screen: the server diffs the result and sends a patch, and the client cache applies it
rows.note: Both other stacks can push the new state in the event itself, but then the event has to be shaped for each screen that listens.

rows.aspect: A board someone else is changing
rows.unit: bytes to keep an open board correct after one move
rows.REST: 56,628 B: the event carries an id, so the client fetches all six columns again
rows.GraphQL: 21,529 B: the subscription carries the event, so the client runs the board query again
rows.Rayfold: 692 B: the server diffs the board it already served and sends the row that moved and the two counts that changed
rows.note: The client asks for nothing: it holds one live query, and what a change costs depends on the change rather than on the size of the screen.
